frames.caption: Find the longest path of strictly increasing values, moving up, down, left or right. There is no fixed fill order: a cell depends on whichever neighbours are larger.
But moves only go to larger values, so a path can never loop back. That means memoised DFS works: len(cell) = 1 + max(len(larger neighbour)), computed once per cell.
Cell (0, 0) with value 9: no larger neighbour, so the path starting here has length 1.
Cell (0, 1) with value 9: no larger neighbour, so the path starting here has length 1.
Cell (1, 2) with value 8: no larger neighbour, so the path starting here has length 1.
Cell (0, 2) with value 4: larger neighbours already solved (1, 1); take the longest + 1.
Cell (1, 0) with value 6: larger neighbours already solved (1); take the longest + 1.
Cell (1, 1) with value 6: larger neighbours already solved (1, 1); take the longest + 1.
Cell (2, 0) with value 2: larger neighbours already solved (2); take the longest + 1.
Cell (2, 1) with value 1: larger neighbours already solved (2, 3); take the longest + 1.
Cell (2, 2) with value 1: larger neighbours already solved (1); take the longest + 1.
Longest increasing path has length 4: 1 → 2 → 6 → 9. Each cell was solved exactly once.
